summary: Delayed initial response and mid-request disconnects traced to reverse-proxy buffer exhaustion on oversized metadata headers
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observe long delays to first byte (often 10–40s) for streaming completions and intermittent connection termination mid-stream. This appears correlated with requests that carry large, repeated metadata headers (distributed tracing + custom tenant routing headers) and slow initial client upload patterns. Impact: production traffic for Beacon Health Analytics (Dedicated) experiences degraded UX and occasional failed completions (~3–7% of streaming sessions during peak).

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east inference plane behind internal edge-proxy fleet (nginx 1.20 variant + custom proxy layer) -> API gateway -> serving runtime.
- Customer on Dedicated capacity, model pins to gpt-open-compat-30b.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client opens streaming completion and attaches heavy tracing/metadata headers (~3–6KB total) across multiple hop headers (x-baggage, x-trace, x-tenant-meta).
2) Client uploads prompt slowly (small chunks over ~2–6s).
3) Edge proxy aggregates headers and buffers request body while awaiting end of client chunking; buffer memory allocation is hit and NGINX proxy_buffering begins to coalesce writes.
4) First byte to client is delayed until proxy flush threshold or timeout (observed ~20–30s in some traces).
5) In certain cases, the proxy or ALB tears down the upstream after crossing an internal idle/send timeout resulting in mid-stream disconnects (client gets ECONNRESET / 502).

Logs/Telemetry:
- Traces: internal request IDs 2026-03-10T14:21:xxZ (trace-id: 7f1a-...), associated with customer session ids BH-9932-*.
- Proxy metrics: proxy_buffer_busy_time spiked for these requests; downstream socket send buffer growth and multiple small write syscalls observed.
- Edge proxy error logs show repeated "upstream prematurely closed connection" entries and "client aborted" entries correlated with requests carrying >4KB of combined metadata headers.

Notes: This differs from previous header-growth incidents because the trigger here is both large combined metadata headers and slow-chunked body upload; the proxy behavior is to hold and coalesce which amplifies send latency and then hits idle/send prune thresholds configured in fronting load balancers.
steps_to_reproduce: Send a streaming completion with large distributed-tracing and tenant headers totaling >3KB while uploading prompt body in 100–500B chunks at 200–500ms intervals
Observe TTFB delay of 10–40s and check proxy logs for buffer allocations and upstream close messages
Repeat with smaller headers or fast single-shot upload — problem does not reproduce consistently
comments: Aisha Kumar (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported spike in failed streaming completions during morning ingest window. Provided initial traces and asked for SRE assistance.

Marcus Lee (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging with a test harness that replays customer headers + chunked upload. Confirmed TTFB delay and proxy buffering behavior. Noted nginx proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size hover near default in edge image.

Marcus Lee (SRE) 2026-03-11: Temporarily disabled proxy_buffering for a narrow route in staging; immediate improvement in TTFB and no mid-stream disconnects. Need coordinated rollout and risk review before prod change.
Customer (Beacon Health) 2026-03-11: Able to confirm reduced failures when client switches to single-shot upload; asks whether platform can accept chunked uploads reliably without client changes.
Product (Lana Cho) 2026-03-12: Needs impact summary and recommended mitigations (config + client guidance) to share with customer success.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: proxy internal buffering + slow client upload causes upstream write coalescing; combined with load balancer idle/send pruning this yields long TTFB and sometimes upstream termination.
Observed nginx config: proxy_buffering on by default; proxy_buffers and proxy_busy_buffers_size set to conservative values for memory control in edge fleet.
ALB/ELB (fronting load balancer) has hard idle/send timeouts that will close connections after no observed bytes for configured window; when proxy holds bytes instead of flushing, ALB triggers prune.
Staging change: disabled proxy_buffering on specific streaming route — confirmed fixe for both TTFB and mid-stream disconnects. No regression in throughput seen in the narrow test run.
Risk: disabling buffering increases number of small write syscalls and could raise CPU on high-concurrency nodes; need to estimate cost impact for Dedicated pool sizing.
Alternate mitigation: increase proxy_buffer sizes and reduce proxy coalescing thresholds, and tune upstream idle/send timeouts where possible.
related_confluence_pages: Confluence: Edge Proxy Runbook - buffering tuning
Confluence: Streaming API SLOs and Load Balancer Guidance
resolution: Temporary workaround: customer switched to single-shot uploads for critical traffic which reduced failures (confirmed).

Short-term fix (canary): disabled proxy_buffering for /v1/streaming-completions route in staging and a small canary in prod (10% of traffic) — observed 90% reduction in TTFB incidents for canary traffic.

Mid-term plan: coordinate with Infra to roll out proxy_buffering=off for streaming routes in Dedicated clusters + add autoscaling margin for CPU/memory increased write syscall cost. Also increase proxy_busy_buffers_size to handle edge cases.

Long-term: implement explicit backpressure-aware flush signals from gateway to edge-proxy and document recommended client chunk sizes; add automated detection on proxy metrics to trigger dynamic tuning.
